Sam (Sales): Quick heads-up — customer wants PO executed + e-sign today. Their procurement team is insisting on cryptographic signer proof (cert chain) and Net30 EOM on the orderform. Can legal/finance confirm we can accept DocuSign cert + audit trail as sufficient? :clock1:
Priya (Legal): We can accept DocuSign audit trail + signing certificate fingerprint as proof for most customers. If they demand bank letter or notarized wet-ink, escalate and we'll review case-by-case. Need to confirm exact wording they want in MSA about "authorized signer."
Alex (Finance): Net30 EOM is fine. We need billing contact, PO number, and tax ID to attach to invoice. If invoice goes into their AP portal, include the portal ID or we'll email acctspay@cust.example. Also: for revenue recognition we need signed order + MSA before we can invoice.
Rina (Procurement): Their vendor onboarding team says "must have chain of trust" and will accept the cert thumbprint + issuer details from the e-sign envelope. They asked for a short attestation statement: "Signed by authorized procurement officer; e-sign certificate attached." Can we add that as a cover page?
Elliot (Eng): No technical blockers. If they ask about KMS/HSM usage for key storage of our signing keys — that's internal, we can provide SOC2 Type II report summary and a description of key management practices, but not private keys. For private deployments, we can provide additional CA artifacts under an NDA.
docusign-bot: Envelope abc-2024-09 submitted by sam@redwood.ai 4:39UTC  status: awaiting signature. https://app.docusign.com/envelope/abc-2024-09
Sam (Sales): Proposed steps: 1) Priya to draft one-line authorized-signer clause we can attach to the order cover. 2) Alex to confirm invoice routing and prepare draft invoice once signed. 3) Rina to confirm procurement's acceptance criteria (exact cert fields). 4) I'll prep DocuSign envelope with PO and the cover attestation. Target: send by noon and close today.
Priya (Legal): Draft clause suggestion: "Authorized Signer: The signatory executing this Order Form on behalf of Customer represents and warrants that they are an officer or an authorized procurement representative. The Parties agree that evidentiary proof consisting of the e-signature envelope audit trail and signing certificate (including issuer and thumbprint) shall constitute prima facie evidence of authorization." Thoughts?
Alex (Finance): Looks good. Confirming billing contact: `payments@cust.example` and tax ID `98-7654321`. They said portal-only for invoices > $200k, so we'll email this one. Alex (Finance): Also confirm PO number they'll issue: `PO-90012`
Rina (Procurement): Procurement confirms they only need: certificate issuer, certificate serial/thumbprint, signing timestamp, and envelope audit-trail pdf. If you include the one-line attestation as a separate PDF in the envelope, vendor team will mark it approved.
Sam (Sales): Adding attestation page + PO-90012 to envelope now. attaching draft order: "Redwood Inference Order Form \nCustomer: Customer Co.\nPO: PO-90012\nTerm: 12 mo\nBilling: Net30 EOM\nPlan: Dedicated 2xA40\nPrice: $35,000/mo"
Priya (Legal): I'll also attach a one-page redline summary of the MSA/DPA changes (SLA tweak and signer clause). Keep it lightweight so procurement can consume quickly.
docusign-bot: Envelope abc-2024-09 signed by `Melinda R.` (procurement) at 2391110064  audit-trail & cert metadata attached. status: completed.
Sam (Sales): Awesome, signed. Next: Alex will issue invoice, Priya to finalize MSA based on the summary and upload final docs to the contract folder, Rina to update vendor onboarding. Thanks team! :tada:
